summary: The current failures point to decimal rounding in the floating-point formatter’s fast path: fixed formatting at precision zero and higher-precision rounding both produce excess upward rounding. The supplied excerpt omits enough of that path to identify the cause confidently.
hypotheses: The fast path rounds an exact halfway value upward at precision zero instead of applying the formatter’s tie-breaking rule.
The fast path’s rounding increment or carry handling changes the retained digit by two, causing excess rounding at higher precisions.
Precision adjustment or fast-path selection gives fixed and general formats an incorrect number of retained digits.
